length.text: Usually under 75 cm; about 85 cm on average

overview.text: The Nose-horned Viper is a venomous viper of south-eastern Europe and western Asia, with a soft 'horn' on the tip of its nose. It is thought to be the most dangerous European viper, with long fangs (up to 13 mm) and strong venom.

size.label: Adults
size.text: About 85 cm on average, though most are under 75 cm; northern snakes are bigger than southern ones.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: North-eastern Italy, southern Austria, the Balkans, Romania, Bulgaria, Greece, Turkey, Georgia, Azerbaijan and Syria.

habitat.text: Dry, rocky hillsides with few plants; sometimes the edges and clearings of woods. Despite its other name, 'sand viper', it does not live in sandy places.

recognise.text: Soft horn on the tip of the snout.
